title: Open Complexity Problem (2-F-PFC for oriented trees of maximum degree ≥ 3)
statement_text: Let $F$ be an oriented tree whose underlying undirected tree has maximum degree at least $3$. The complexity of the $2$-$F$-PFC (deciding whether a given planar digraph admits an $F$-free $2$-coloring) remains partially open. In particular, the complexity for those $F$ where successively deleting all leaves yields a star $K_{1,n}$ is not determined.
context_text: Digraphs are simple (orientations of graphs). A digraph is $F$-free if it has no induced subdigraph isomorphic to $F$, and a coloring $c:V(D)\to\{0,\dots,k-1\}$ is an $F$-free $k$-coloring if every color class induces an $F$-free subdigraph. The problem $k$-$F$-PFC (planar $F$-free $k$-coloring) asks, for fixed $F$ and $k$, whether a given planar digraph admits an $F$-free $k$-coloring. It is trivial for $k\ge4$ by the Four Color Theorem, polynomial whenever $F$ contains a (not necessarily directed) cycle (planar graphs admit $C_n$-free 2-colorings), and for $k=3$ every planar digraph has an $F$-free 3-coloring when $F$ has maximum degree at least 3 (planar graphs can be partitioned into 3 induced linear forests); so the interesting case is $F$ an oriented tree and $k\in\{2,3\}$. The authors prove that for every orientation $\vec P$ of the path $P_n$, the $2$-$\vec P$-PFC is polynomial for $n\le2$ and NP-complete for $n\ge3$, and the $3$-$\vec P$-PFC is polynomial for $n=1$ and NP-complete for $n\ge2$, even for acyclic inputs. Writing $\mathrm{lrem}(\vec T)$ for the oriented tree obtained from $\vec T$ by deleting all its leaves, they show that the $2$-$\mathrm{lrem}(\vec T)$-PFC reduces polynomially to the $2$-$\vec T$-PFC; hence the $2$-$F$-PFC is NP-hard whenever iterating $\mathrm{lrem}$ on $F$ reaches an oriented path of length 2 or 3 (number of edges). The remaining case is when iterating $\mathrm{lrem}$ reaches a star $K_{1,n}$. For undirected graphs, Broersma, Fomin, Kratochvíl and Woeginger showed that planar $F$-free 2-coloring is NP-hard if $F$ is a tree with at least two edges.
